title: MSBuild project execution by a self-hosted CI build agent

alert.rule_name: Defense Evasion: MSBuild Executed a Project File From a Non-Development Path

mitre_attack.technique: T1127.001 - Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution: MSBuild

alert.description: MSBuild.exe executed a project file located outside any recognised source-code or build-agent path. MSBuild is a signed Microsoft binary that will compile and run arbitrary C# supplied inline in a project file, so it is used to execute code on hosts where unsigned binaries would be blocked or noticed.
alert.detection_logic: Sysmon EventID=1 (ProcessCreate) WHERE Image ENDSWITH '\MSBuild.exe' AND CommandLine MATCHES '\.(xml|csproj|proj|targets)' AND CommandLine NOT MATCHES ANY (source_root_paths, build_agent_paths, '\Program Files')

enrichment.workspace_path: C:\a\1\s is the default working directory of a self-hosted Azure Pipelines agent: 'a' is the agent work root, '1' is the agent's numeric work folder for this pipeline, and 's' is the sources directory. The short path is chosen by the agent to avoid Windows MAX_PATH limits during builds. The detection allowlist covers \source\repos and Program Files but not agent work roots, which is why this fired.
enrichment.process_lineage: The chain is Agent.Listener.exe (running as a service) -> Agent.Worker.exe -> cmd.exe -> MSBuild.exe. Agent.Listener is the long-lived agent service; Agent.Worker is the per-job process it forks. There is no remote-execution parent anywhere in the chain.
enrichment.source_provenance: The project file MSBuild consumed was created 0.7 seconds earlier by git.exe, running under the same agent worker, as part of 'git checkout --progress --force 3f9c1a7d…'. Its provenance is a source-control checkout of a specific commit, not a file placed on the host by another machine.
enrichment.network_context: The only outbound connection from the agent is to dev.azure.com on TCP/443 — the pipeline service the agent polls for work. No connection to an unrecognised address appears in the window.
enrichment.compilation_artifacts: MSBuild spawns csc.exe and cvtres.exe and writes .cs, .dll, .pdb and .cmdline files under the project's own obj\Release directory. Compiler invocation is not by itself suspicious: it is what a build is. What matters is that the outputs land in the project tree, named after the project, rather than in randomly-named directories under a user's Temp folder.
enrichment.account: THESHIRE\svc-build is the account the agent service runs as, in terminal session 0. It is a service account, not an interactive user, and the same account owns every process in the chain.
enrichment.what_is_absent: No SMB share writes, no remote process creation, no encoded or hidden-window PowerShell, no unsigned binaries, and no connection to any address outside the expected pipeline endpoint.

verdict.rationale: The corrected target-host lineage, source-control checkout, agent workspace, and ordinary compiler outputs strongly resemble a CI build. However, an evidence-bounded SOC analyst has no pipeline authorization, change record, repository trust, or project-content validation, and MSBuild can execute inline code from the checked-out project. The activity therefore warrants customer confirmation before closure rather than being labeled benign solely from its intended construction.

observations.desc: The build-launching cmd.exe invoked MSBuild.exe against that project, and MSBuild.exe started at 21:39:24.350 under CORP\svc-build.
The subsequent target-host chain includes csc.exe and cvtres.exe and writes Contoso.Billing.dll and Contoso.Billing.pdb under the project's obj\Release directory.

inferences.desc: The corrected Agent.Listener -> Agent.Worker -> cmd -> MSBuild lineage, checkout provenance, and project-local compiler outputs are consistent with an automated CI build.
Execution of a checked-out project by MSBuild could also execute inline build tasks, so normal-looking compiler behavior does not establish benign project content.
The provided target-host window does not establish whether commit 3f9c1a7d was approved, whether the job was expected, or whether the agent or repository was compromised.

investigations.desc: Ask the customer to confirm that WKS-4472, CORP\svc-build, and build job 3f9c1a were authorized at the observed time.
Inspect commit 3f9c1a7d and Contoso.Billing.csproj for inline tasks, unusual targets, downloaded content, or post-build execution.
Validate the agent registration, listener configuration, and pipeline run metadata against the customer's CI inventory.
Review target-host activity after 21:39:29.2 for execution of build outputs, persistence, or unexpected network connections.
If the job is confirmed, tune the rule using both the approved agent lineage and workspace root rather than a path-only exclusion.
